newsitem.title: GHANA: Libyan plane landed in Ghana - airport source. [CORRECTED 17:35 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Libyan plane landed in Ghana - airport source. [CORRECTED 17:35 GMT]

text.p: A Libyan plane landed in Accra airport on Tuesday and left the Ghanaian capital less than three hours later, a source at Accra airport said on Wednesday.
"A Libyan Boeing 727 (corrects from 747) arrived here at 8.39 p.m. (2039 GMT) yesterday and left at 11 p.m.," said the source who was at the airport then.
Officials later removed records of the flight, added the source, who asked not to be named.

Libya said on Wednesday a Libyan aircraft had flown a Libyan foreign ministry delegation to Accra despite a 1992 United Nations ban on its international flights. The official Libyan news agency JANA, monitored in Tunis, said an adviser to President Jerry Rawlings and a Ghanaian foreign ministry official greeted the delegation at the airport.

But a senior Ghanaian foreign ministry official said he had no knowledge of a Libyan visit. "I am not aware of the visit of a Libyan delegation, and I was with the deputy foreign minister up to 2 p.m. today," said Kobina Wudu, head of the ministry's Organisation of African Unity desk.
One official of the foreign ministry's protocol service said his department had been told earlier to expect a Libyan delegation but none had turned up.
A Libyan delegation headed by Foreign Minister Omar Mustafa al-Montasser has been touring West Africa and was last known to be in Zaire on Tuesday.
